question: What are the most important signal generation capabilities for applications in AI?
answer: The Vault contains no note that ranks or defines "the most important signal generation capabilities for applications in AI" — there is no AI-specific signal-generator requirements page. The only place signal generation is tied to an AI-adjacent application area is the high-speed digital / AI-server test material: the 2026.3.4 R&S high-speed digital deck (whose context is the Taiwan AI server eco-chain) maps signal generators to just two validation blocks — RefClk and PLL jitter performance (together with phase noise analyzers) and ADC/DAC frontend performance (together with spectrum analyzers). That source gives instrument categories only, with no models, bandwidths, jitter masks, phase-noise offsets or ADC/DAC figures, and the Vault explicitly warns these instrument types must not be turned into formal product configurations. The Vault's actual AI/ML wireless content is about AI-enhanced CSI feedback with a two-sided AI model, where the test instrument is the R&S CMX500 acting as an AI-enabled base station emulator — not a signal generator. Where the Vault does enumerate concrete signal generation capabilities (R&S SMW200A: LTE, Cellular IoT, 5G NR R17/18 K171, OFDM signal generation K114, custom digital modulation, fading/Doppler/path delay), the application context is 3GPP NTN, not AI. So the question cannot be answered from the Vault beyond the two instrument-category pointers above.
missing: The Vault has no note, datasheet section, or application brochure that states which signal generation capabilities matter most for AI applications — no AI-specific requirements on modulation bandwidth, phase noise/jitter, multi-channel/MIMO, fading, waveform/arbitrary-waveform generation, clock generation for AI accelerators, or generating RF datasets for AI/ML training. It also lacks any AI-context signal generator specification values (jitter masks, phase-noise offsets, ADC/DAC frontend figures, data rates) and any R&S application note mapping signal generators to AI data-center, AI-server, or AI/ML wireless test use cases beyond the two instrument-category pointers in the 2026.3.4 high-speed digital deck.
